title: Jio Targets September 2027 Test Launch for 1,600-Satellite LEO Network
excerpt: Reliance Jio plans to deploy a handful of test satellites before mass rollout in early 2028, aiming to build India's first homegrown LEO broadband constellation with 4.8 Tbps capacity.
body:
• Reliance Jio targets September 2027 for a test launch of satellites for its planned 1,600-satellite LEO constellation, with mass deployment set for early 2028.
  • Each satellite will operate at 650 km altitude with 100–150 Gbps capacity; the full network would deliver 4–4.8 Tbps over India, exceeding Starlink's approved 600 Gbps.
  • India's space regulator IN-SPACe cleared the plan as "technically sound" in July 2026 after a joint review with ISRO and the Department of Telecommunications.
  • Jio Platforms' upcoming IPO could raise roughly $3.8 billion, with funds partly earmarked for satellite and technology investments.

Reliance Jio is targeting September 2027 for the test launch of satellites for its proposed 1,600-satellite low Earth orbit constellation, according to sources cited by the Economic Times. The move marks the telecom giant's most concrete step yet toward building India's first homegrown satellite broadband network.

The test launch will involve placing a small number of satellites in orbit to evaluate the network's hardware, software, and operational systems before mass deployment begins in early 2028. Jio has filed an application with the International Telecommunication Union for the orbital resources required for the network.

The Deployment Roadmap

After the test flight, Jio plans to send 90 to 100 minimum-coverage satellites into orbit within two to three quarters, enough for India to start receiving satellite connectivity in 2028. The company aims to have 400 to 450 satellites deployed by 2030 and to complete the full 1,600-satellite constellation by 2035.

The satellites will operate at approximately 650 km altitude — slightly higher than Starlink and Amazon's Project Kuiper — with each unit offering throughput of 100 to 150 Gbps. At full capacity, roughly 30 to 32 satellites would be positioned over India at any given time, providing aggregate capacity of 4 to 4.8 Tbps.

That would exceed the capacity proposed by other LEO operators targeting India. Starlink's approved capacity stands at around 600 Gbps, while Amazon's Project Kuiper has reportedly sought approval for about 3 Tbps, according to the Economic Times.

Regulatory Clearance

The plan received a critical approval in July 2026 when IN-SPACe — the Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre — found Jio's constellation plan "technically sound" after a joint evaluation with the Indian Space Research Organisation and the Department of Telecommunications. The clearance allows the government to extend regulatory backing to Jio at the international level, including support for ITU filings and coordination of orbital rights with other satellite operators.

"Around 90-100 minimum coverage satellites are planned to be sent in two-three quarters after the test launch, which means India can start getting satellite connectivity in 2028."

— Source familiar with the plans, cited by Economic Times

IN-SPACe has also flagged the defense potential of the constellation, with discussions underway about hosting defense payloads on some of the satellites, according to Outlook Business.

Competition in India's Satcom Market

Jio's constellation would add another major player to India's rapidly developing satellite communications market. Elon Musk's Starlink and Bharti Enterprises-backed Eutelsat OneWeb both hold provisional licenses in India and are waiting for final spectrum allocation. Amazon's Project Kuiper is also preparing to enter the market.

Jio's push builds on its existing partnership with Luxembourg-based satellite operator SES through their joint venture Jio Space Technology Limited. Jio Platforms Managing Director Akash Ambani has said the company plans to work with global constellation operators while developing its own capabilities and building ground stations across India.

The IPO Factor

The satellite play comes as Jio Platforms gears up for its IPO. India's markets regulator approved the draft prospectus at the end of August, setting up a listing that could raise approximately $3.8 billion. A portion of those funds is expected to go toward technology investments, including the satellite constellation. The government has opted for administrative allocation of satellite spectrum rather than auctions and is working on pricing and conditions governing the assignment.

For investors in the Indian diaspora, the Jio Platforms IPO represents one of the year's most closely watched offerings, combining the company's dominant telecom position with its emerging ambitions in satellite broadband and enterprise connectivity.
nri_angle: Jio's satellite constellation signals its evolution from a domestic telecom disruptor into a space-technology player, with potential implications for connectivity across South Asia and investment opportunities via the upcoming Jio Platforms IPO.
